neighbours.label: ' with' in the hedging idiom 'treat/take/view X with caution' or 'with a grain of salt' (the slot before a caution/doubt word)
fire: These survey results should be treated with caution because the sample was tiny.
Any claim from an anonymous forum post must be taken with a grain of salt.
The estimates for the rural districts should be viewed with some caution.
Investors were told to interpret the quarterly forecast with great caution.
Figures from that period must be handled with care, as many records were lost.
Honestly, I would take his travel advice with a pinch of salt.
The authors warn that their model's predictions should be used with caution.
Reports of the miracle cure ought to be approached with healthy caution.
quiet: These wounds should be treated with iodine because the cut was deep.
The tablets must be taken with a glass of water after every meal.
The rural districts can be viewed with binoculars from the old tower.
Investors were told to fill in the quarterly forms with a black pen.
Fragile parcels must be packed with foam, as many boxes were crushed.
Honestly, I would season the potatoes with a pinch of salt.
The authors explain that their model was trained with data from 2019.
The old chapel ought to be restored with stone from the local quarry.

notes: card: peaks on ' with' in 'treated with a large grain of salt', 'taken with some caution', 'treated with caution', and ' unsus(pecting)'; - pole is 'sin duda / sans doute / kein Zweifel' and output suppresses doubt words. Probe: 'read with caution' 0.79, 'treated with antibiotics' 0.01, 'greeted with skepticism' only 0.04. Near misses use 'with' in literal senses.
